newsitem.title: HONDURAS: Two U.S. women killed in Honduras flooding.
newsitem.headline: Two U.S. women killed in Honduras flooding.

text.p: Two American women working for the Peace Corps were killed on Friday after being swept away by a raging river in Honduras, the U.S. embassy said.
This Central American country has been subject to intense flooding from unrelenting rain the past two weeks, leaving four Hondurans dead.
The embassy said it could not identify the women or provide their hometowns pending notification of their families.

"Two U.S. citizens, one of them a Peace Corps volunteer and one an instructor for the organisation based in Honduras, drowned while trying to cross the Quiscamote River," the embassy said in a press bulletin.
Honduran police identified the two as Anica Rodriguez, 22, and Catalina de Martinez, 20.
"Both women were pulled away by the waters of the Quiscamote River," police Capt. Jose Enamourado told Reuters.
The accident occurred near the town of Union, about 90 miles (150 km) east of Tegucigalpa.
Firefighters said they were searching for the body of another potential victim of the flooding, a Honduran man, in the Choluteca River near Tegucigalpa.
In the city of Choluteca, about 60 miles (100 km) south of Tegucigalpa, authorities said they were evacuating more than 20 families from their homes near the banks of the river.
